result.summary: The image shows a dense urban corridor with wide, well-maintained sidewalks but a lack of marked pedestrian crossings at a wide intersection. The multi-lane, one-way street configuration suggests a focus on vehicle throughput, which increases pedestrian exposure and potential traffic speeds.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crosswalk
hazards.description: The intersection lacks painted crosswalks, making pedestrian crossing points less predictable for drivers.

hazards.name: Wide Multi-lane Roadway
hazards.description: Three or more travel lanes increase the distance pedestrians must cross and can encourage higher vehicle speeds.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install zebra or ladder style pavement markings to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the intersection to shorten crossing distance and improve sight lines.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install signals that show the remaining time to cross, improving pedestrian decision-making.

result.summary: This urban intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure like sidewalks, curb ramps, and signals, but lacks any visible pavement markings. The wide, unmarked expanse of asphalt increases pedestrian exposure and may encourage higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Unmarked crosswalk
hazards.description: The intersection lacks painted crosswalks, which reduces driver awareness and fails to provide a designated path for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Wide unmarked roadway
hazards.description: The absence of lane markings on a wide street can lead to higher vehicle speeds and unpredictable driver behavior.

interventions.title: High-visibility crosswalks

interventions.title: Curb extensions

interventions.title: Lane markings

result.summary: The intersection features a high-visibility brick-textured crosswalk, pedestrian signals, and well-maintained sidewalks in a dense urban environment. While basic safety infrastructure is present, the wide roadway and lack of physical buffers like curb extensions or medians leave pedestrians exposed to traffic over a significant crossing distance.

hazards.name: Wide street profile
hazards.description: The relatively wide, open roadway design may encourage higher vehicle speeds despite the urban context.

hazards.name: Lack of physical protection at corners
hazards.description: The corners lack bollards or hardened features to protect pedestrians from vehicle encroachment during turns.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and slow turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles get a green light.

interventions.title: Bicycle Infrastructure
interventions.description: Add protected bike lanes to further narrow the travel lanes and provide a buffer for pedestrians.
